Twenty.description: Twenty provides per-tenant generated REST and GraphQL APIs for core CRM objects and custom objects. API keys are created via Settings → API & Webhooks.
Twenty.notes: Authentication method inferred from mention of creating an API key; no explicit auth method list provided.

Salesforce.description: Salesforce provides multiple public APIs (SOAP, Connect REST, Streaming) with OAuth 2.0 authentication via Connected Apps. Free Developer Edition allows self‑service sign‑up and creation of connected apps. Hosted MCP servers are available.
Salesforce.notes: OAuth 2.0 is the primary auth method; SOAP login uses session ID token but not classified under listed categories.

HubSpot.description: HubSpot's public API (api.hubapi.com) supports OAuth for multi-account/public apps and static/private app access tokens for single-account use. Auth is via Bearer token in the Authorization header. The API covers CRM objects (contacts, deals, engagements), and HubSpot provides a developer platform, CLI tooling, and usage/limit guidelines.
HubSpot.mcp_notes: Official HubSpot MCP servers exist: a Remote HubSpot MCP server (read/write CRM data) and a local Developer MCP server. See https://developers.hubspot.com/ai-tools/mcp
HubSpot.notes: Access model inferred: HubSpot offers a free tier and self-serve developer account where private app access tokens can be generated without sales approval; text does not explicitly state pricing, so free_signup is a reasonable but not fully confirmed classification. 'api_key' used to represent the static/private app access token (Bearer token). OAuth is required for Marketplace/multi-customer apps.

Pipedrive.description: Pipedrive offers a RESTful API v1 with token-based and OAuth 2.0 authentication, free for all plans, and includes a native MCP server for AI assistants.
Pipedrive.notes: API token is tied to a specific user and company; only one active token at a time. OAuth 2.0 is required for marketplace apps.

Attio.description: Attio is a flexible, data-driven CRM for managing contacts, companies, deals, and workflows. It provides a public REST API that exchanges JSON over HTTPS, with authentication via OAuth 2.0 or single-workspace API keys.
Attio.mcp_notes: Official hosted MCP server at https://mcp.attio.com/mcp (docs at https://docs.attio.com/mcp/overview); also listed on mcp.so. Connects via OAuth.
blockers: API key creation requires workspace admin access
Attio.notes: API key generation requires workspace admin privileges (admin must create the token in Workspace settings > Developers). OAuth 2.0 is the preferred method for multi-workspace apps. API is available on all plans.

Podio.description: Podio provides a complete REST API with OAuth2 authentication and self‑serve API key generation. Developers can sign up for a free Podio account, register an app, and obtain a client ID/secret to access the API. An official MCP server (https://mcp.podio.com) is available for AI assistant integration.
Podio.notes: API key generation is done via the Podio account settings; no paid plan is required for basic API access.

Zoho CRM.description: Zoho CRM provides a RESTful API (v2) that uses OAuth 2.0 for authentication, supporting JSON payloads and standard HTTP methods. It also offers a client credentials flow for server‑to‑server tasks. Zoho additionally offers Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for AI integration.
Zoho CRM.notes: The documentation does not specify whether API access is available on the free tier or requires a paid plan.

Close.description: Close is a CRM/sales platform with a well-documented REST API (base URL https://api.close.com/api/v1) covering leads, contacts, opportunities, activities, and custom fields. It supports API keys (via HTTP Basic Auth) and OAuth 2.0, with pagination, field selection, and rate limiting.
Close.mcp_notes: Official MCP server referenced in Close's own docs (llms.txt): "connect to the MCP server at https://developer.close.com/_mcp/server".
Close.notes: API keys are created in-app under Settings → Developer → API Keys, so a developer with a Close account can self-serve credentials. However, the text does not state whether a Close account itself is free or requires a paid plan, so access_model is left as unknown. The MCP server is explicitly mentioned in the product's own llms.txt, so has_mcp is true.

Copper.description: Copper CRM exposes a Developer API accessible via two methods: API keys (token-based, generated in the Copper web app under System settings > API Keys, suitable for individual users) and OAuth2.0 (Authorization Code Grant flow, preferred for partner/third-party integrations). API keys require the token plus the user's email in request headers; OAuth requires registering an application with Copper to obtain client_id and client_secret.
Copper.mcp_notes: Unofficial third-party MCP server found: hasankhadra/copper-mcp (GitHub, MIT, read-heavy with one guarded write tool). No official Copper MCP mentioned.
blockers: OAuth2.0 app registration requires contacting partners@copper.com (not self-serve)
Copper.notes: Two distinct auth paths: API keys are self-serve (generate in-app, no approval), but OAuth2.0 requires contacting partners@copper.com to register an application and receive client_id/client_secret. The docs describe API keys as 'legacy' relative to OAuth. Access model set to freemium as a reasonable inference (Copper is a paid CRM with a free tier) but the scraped text does not explicitly state pricing/free-tier API access — worth double-checking.

DealCloud.description: DealCloud provides a REST API secured via OAuth2 client credentials flow and API keys. Access requires being a user within a DealCloud organization with appropriate permissions, typically an enterprise/paid plan.
blockers: requires admin-enabled API key or client credentials
enterprise plan required
DealCloud.notes: MCP server is in client preview starting July 2026, not yet generally available.

Zendesk.description: Zendesk provides a comprehensive REST API. Authentication primarily via OAuth2 access tokens; API tokens and basic auth are also mentioned (deprecated). Developers can obtain OAuth credentials via the admin interface with a Zendesk account.
Zendesk.notes: Access model not explicitly described; assumes free trial possible but not stated. API token considered as api_key.

Intercom.description: Intercom provides a REST API with OAuth2 for public apps and Access Tokens (Bearer token) for private apps. Developers can create apps in the Developer Hub and obtain credentials instantly, with free development workspaces available.
Intercom.notes: Public app access is free via development workspace; private app requires a paid Intercom workspace but token is still self-serve.

Freshdesk.description: Freshdesk provides a well-documented REST v2 API secured with an API key using Basic authentication. API keys can be generated by users themselves. No OAuth support currently.
Freshdesk.notes: Access model not clearly defined; Freshdesk may require a paid subscription, but documentation does not specify.

Front.description: Front provides a Core REST API authenticated via Bearer tokens (API tokens) or OAuth2. Developers can sign up for a free developer account, obtain API tokens (admin required) or OAuth credentials, and use the well-documented REST endpoints.
Front.mcp_notes: Front MCP server (open beta) at https://dev.frontapp.com/docs/mcp-server
blockers: admin privileges required to create API token for private use
Front.notes: Public integrations for all Front customers must use OAuth; private integrations can use API tokens. MCP server is in open beta and available to all.

Pylon.description: Pylon provides a REST API secured via Bearer token (API key) generated in the dashboard. Developers can self‑serve tokens without sales contact. Documentation describes many endpoints. An MCP server exists at https://mcp.usepylon.com using OAuth 2.0.
Pylon.mcp_notes: Pylon MCP Server at https://mcp.usepylon.com (OAuth 2.0 AuthKit)
Pylon.notes: Pricing and whether a free tier exists are not described, so access model is unclear.

LiveAgent.description: LiveAgent provides a REST API (v3) authenticated via API key passed in request header. API keys are generated in admin configuration. Public documentation and Swagger-generated client exist. MCP server is available for AI tool integration.
LiveAgent.notes: Pricing and whether free signup grants API access not specified; access model set to unknown.

Plain.description: Plain offers a GraphQL API authenticated via Machine User API keys (Bearer token). Developers can create machine users and API keys via the UI without sales contact.
Plain.notes: API access may require an existing Plain account, possibly a paid plan; not explicitly stated.

Help Scout.description: Help Scout provides OAuth2 (Authorization Code and Client Credentials) for its Mailbox API and API key via HTTP Basic Auth for Docs API. Developers can create OAuth2 apps and generate API keys via their profile without sales contact.
Help Scout.notes: Access model not explicitly described; assume unknown. API appears to be a broad REST API covering inbox, docs, etc.

Gorgias.description: Gorgias provides a REST API that can be accessed via HTTP Basic Auth using an API key for private apps, or via OAuth2 bearer tokens for public apps. API keys are tied to a user and can be generated in the account settings. OAuth2 supports scopes and refresh tokens. The API is well documented with example curl requests.
Gorgias.notes: Access model (free vs paid) is not specified in the documentation; likely requires a paid plan but not confirmed.

Gladly.description: Gladly provides a REST API (HTTPS at {organization}.gladly.com) for managing customer profile data, customer timelines, and order information, plus a Lookup API for providing data services to agents. Responses/payloads are JSON with consistent error codes. API tokens are required for authentication and are created in the Gladly UI by users with the API User role.
Gladly.mcp_notes: Third-party managed MCP servers exist: StackOne (https://www.stackone.com/connectors/gladly/mcp/) and Truto (https://truto.one/blog/connect-gladly-to-claude-sync-customer-profiles-and-inbox-workflows/). No official Gladly MCP mentioned.
blockers: requires a Gladly account
requires admin to create an API User role account
tokens tied to specific environment (Sandbox/Production)
Gladly.notes: API access is gated behind a Gladly account and an admin creating a user with the API User role; tokens are tied to a single user and environment (Sandbox vs Production). Pricing/plan requirements for API access are not stated in the text, so access_model is left unknown.

Slack.description: Slack Web API is a collection of HTTP RPC-style methods (URLs like https://slack.com/api/METHOD_FAMILY.method) for querying and acting on a Slack workspace. It is not a REST API but is HTTP-based, supports GET/POST with form-encoded or JSON bodies, and requires HTTPS/TLS v1.2+. Apps are installed via a v2 OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow, gaining an access token scoped to requested permissions.
Slack.mcp_notes: Official Slack MCP server exists (slack.com/help/articles/48855576908307-Guide-to-Model-Context-Protocol-in-Slack); also referenced by ClickUp blog as an official server for agent access.
Slack.notes: Docs explicitly state the Web API is NOT a REST API (it is HTTP RPC-style), so api_quality 'rich_rest' is used loosely to denote a broad, well-documented HTTP API; a human may prefer 'limited_rest' or a custom label. Auth: OAuth 2.0 (v2 flow) is the primary documented method; 'api_key' is included because the OAuth flow yields an access token used as a bearer token for API calls, but the text does not explicitly describe a standalone API-key signup flow. Access model inferred as free_signup since developers can build/install apps in their own workspace and join the Slack Developer Program for sandboxes without a paid plan; no sales gate mentioned.

Twilio.description: Twilio's REST API (base https://api.twilio.com/2010-04-01) provides programmatic access to communications products: phone numbers, calls, SMS, recordings, and more. Auth is via HTTP Basic authentication using an API key SID as username and API key secret as password (Account SID/Auth Token for local testing). API keys are created in the Twilio Console or via the API. A Twilio MCP server (Public Beta) also exists, giving AI agents access to 1,800+ endpoints across 30+ products.
Twilio.mcp_notes: Official Twilio MCP server exists (Public Beta): https://www.twilio.com/docs/ai/mcp — gives AI agents access to 1,800+ endpoints across 30+ products.
Twilio.notes: Access model inferred as freemium: Twilio offers a free trial/credits for new accounts, but the scraped text does not explicitly state pricing or free-tier details, so this is a reasonable but not text-confirmed assumption. Auth is HTTP Basic using API key SID/secret (so both basic_auth and api_key apply). MCP server is in Public Beta, not GA.

Zoho Cliq.description: Zoho Cliq is a team messaging and collaboration platform with a REST API (v2 and v3) for managing channels, bots, slash commands, message webhooks, chats, and team communications. The API uses resource-oriented URLs, JSON request/response bodies, standard HTTP verbs, and OAuth 2.0 authentication. It supports multi-data center deployments across nine regional domains.
Zoho Cliq.mcp_notes: Official Zoho Cliq MCP server exists; documented at https://www.zoho.com/cliq/help/platform/zoho-cliq-mcp.html and setup guide at https://help.zoho.com/portal/en/kb/zoho-cliq/cliq-7-0/user-guides/articles/setting-up-the-zoho-cliq-mcp-server
Zoho Cliq.notes: Zoho Cliq is part of the Zoho suite; API access is tied to a Zoho account. The text does not explicitly state a free tier, but Zoho Cliq has historically offered a free plan, and OAuth 2.0 self-serve app registration is standard for Zoho APIs. Confidence slightly reduced because the scraped text does not explicitly confirm free signup or trial details.

Lark (Larksuite).description: Lark (Larksuite) provides a RESTful OpenAPI that uses OAuth 2.0 for authentication. Developers can create an app in the Developer Console, apply for permissions, and obtain tenant, app, or user access tokens to call the API. The platform offers a free developer signup and self‑serve credential issuance.
Lark (Larksuite).mcp_notes: Feishu/Lark OpenAPI MCP – GitHub repo: https://github.com/larksuite/lark-openapi-mcp; also documented at https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/mcp_integration/mcp_introduction
blockers: requires permission approval
Lark (Larksuite).notes: The API requires permission approval for each scope; the MCP tool is available in beta.

Pumble.description: Pumble (by CAKE.com) is a team messaging/collaboration app. It offers a public API accessible via an "API addon" that generates API keys for HTTP requests (send messages, reactions, channel creation, listing messages/channels), plus a full OAuth2 app-authorization flow (client_id/client_secret, scopes, redirect) documented in the Pumble Node SDK. Rate limit is 1000 requests/minute/user. An official Pumble MCP server also exists for connecting AI agents (Claude, Gemini, Codex).
Pumble.mcp_notes: Official Pumble MCP server documented at https://pumble.com/help/integrations/automation-workflow-integrations/how-to-use-the-pumble-mcp-server/ — connects Claude, Gemini, Codex to Pumble for search/read/act.
blockers: API addon must be installed on the workspace before generating a key
private channel access requires Addon Bot to be a member
Pumble.notes: Two auth paths: simple API key via the in-app API addon (self-serve, no sales) and a full OAuth2 app flow (client_id/client_secret) per the Node SDK. Access model assumed free_signup since the API addon is installed in-workspace and keys are generated by the user with no mention of paid gating; not 100% certain a free Pumble workspace is required vs. a paid plan, so access_model confidence is moderate. Rate limit 1000 req/min/user.

Discord.description: Discord's public API is accessed via OAuth2 (authorization code, implicit, client credentials, plus bot/webhook flows). Developers register an application to obtain a client_id and client_secret. The API is a broad, well-documented REST interface for the Discord chat platform, with some OAuth2 scopes requiring Discord approval.
Discord.mcp_notes: Third-party MCP servers exist: rayenking/discord-mcp (MIT, stdio) and mine1x/discord-mcp (192-208 tools, Go/TS). No official Discord MCP mentioned in the text.
blockers: Some OAuth2 scopes require Discord approval
Discord.notes: Text confirms self-serve app registration (client_id/client_secret) and a rich REST API. A few OAuth2 scopes are gated behind Discord approval, which could limit certain connector features. MCP servers found are third-party and low-traction (0-1 stars), not official.

Telegram.description: Telegram offers three developer APIs: the Bot API (an HTTP/HTTPS-based interface for building bots, with a simplified version of the Telegram API handled by an intermediary server), the Telegram API/TDLib (for building fully customized clients), and the Gateway API (for sending verification codes). The Bot API is free for developers and supports payments, Mini Apps, and rich messaging.
Telegram.mcp_notes: Multiple third-party MCP servers found: mcp-telegram/mcp-telegram (181 tools, MTProto userbot, self-host via npx or hosted at mcp-telegram.com) and AlexeyPevz/telegram-mcp (MTProto-based MCP server).
Telegram.notes: Bot API uses a bot token (obtained via @BotFather) which functions as an API key. The text does not explicitly name the auth method as 'api_key' but the token-based HTTPS interface strongly implies it. TDLib uses MTProto (custom protocol) rather than REST. The Bot API is the primary self-serve path.

WhatsApp Business.description: WhatsApp Business Platform offers a RESTful Graph API for messaging and calling, authenticated with an OAuth2 bearer token. Developers can create a Meta App, WhatsApp Business account, and use Embedded Signup to onboard clients. The API is billed per message, with no free tier.
WhatsApp Business.mcp_notes: No MCP server found for WhatsApp in the provided sources.
WhatsApp Business.notes: Pricing is per-message; no free tier is mentioned. Self-serve onboarding is available via Embedded Signup.

Aircall.description: Aircall Public API is a classic REST API (root https://api.aircall.io/v1) for accessing Aircall account information (calls, contacts, SMS, users, teams, transcripts, AI insights). Authentication is via Basic Auth (API ID + token generated from the Aircall Dashboard) for your own account, or OAuth for Technology Partners building apps for multiple users / the Aircall App Marketplace.
Aircall.mcp_notes: Two third-party (unofficial) MCP servers found: themobilefirstco/aircall-mcp-server (73 tools, MIT) and growth-box/aircall-mcp (local read-only, MIT). No official Aircall MCP mentioned.
blockers: OAuth/partner flow requires Technology Partner account for multi-tenant apps
App Marketplace listing requires partner approval
Aircall.notes: Basic Auth (API ID + token) is self-serve from the Aircall Dashboard for your own account, so a single-tenant connector is buildable today. OAuth is required for multi-tenant/marketplace apps and needs a partner-specific account. Access model set to freemium (Aircall is a paid telephony product with a free trial); the text does not explicitly state a free API tier, so this is a mild inference. MCP servers are third-party/unofficial, not endorsed by Aircall.

Vonage.description: Vonage provides a comprehensive suite of REST APIs for communications (voice, messaging, video, etc.) with multiple authentication options (API key/secret, JWT, Basic Auth, OAuth2). Developers can sign up for a free account and obtain credentials instantly.
Vonage.notes: SIP Trunking uses Digest Authentication, not captured in standard auth method list.

Google Ads.description: Google Ads API is a comprehensive REST/gRPC API for managing Google Ads campaigns, ad groups, ads, and billing. It requires a developer token (22-char alphanumeric) obtained via the API Center of a Google Ads Manager Account, plus a Google Cloud service account for authentication. Access levels (Test, Basic, Standard) control daily call volume and environment (test vs production).
Google Ads.mcp_notes: Official Google Ads MCP server exists: https://github.com/googleads/google-ads-mcp (Apache 2.0, ~626 stars) and documented at https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/developer-toolkit/mcp-server
blockers: Requires a Google Ads Manager Account (MCC) to apply for a developer token
Developer token starts in Pending status; production access requires approval
Requires a Google Cloud project with a service account and key
Google Ads.notes: Developer token requires a Google Ads Manager Account (MCC) and an application/approval process; newly created tokens start in 'Pending' status and only work against Test Accounts until approved for production. This is a soft gate (self-serve application, not a sales call), but production access is not immediate. Auth uses a developer-token header (custom_token) plus a Google Cloud service account JSON key (api_key). Both REST and gRPC are supported.

Meta Ads.description: Meta Marketing API (Meta Ads) is a REST-based API for managing Facebook/Instagram/WhatsApp ads, campaigns, audiences, and billing. Access requires a Meta Developer account, a created app, and an active ad account. Authentication is via access tokens (user/system) obtained through the Graph API Explorer or Facebook Login for Business. Advanced Access via Meta App Review is required to serve businesses you do not own.
Meta Ads.mcp_notes: Official Meta-hosted Ads MCP Server at https://mcp.facebook.com/ads (released Jul 16, 2026); lets AI agents create/edit/delete campaigns, manage audiences, and query performance.
blockers: Advanced Access via Meta App Review required to serve third-party businesses
requires active ad account for billing
Meta Ads.notes: Auth is token-based (access tokens) via Graph API Explorer; Facebook Login for Business is the OAuth-style flow for business integrations. Self-serve for your own ad account is easy; serving other businesses' accounts is gated behind Meta App Review (Advanced Access). MCP server is official and remote-hosted.

LinkedIn Ads.description: LinkedIn Advertising API provides REST endpoints for managing ad accounts, campaigns, creatives, and analytics. Access requires an approved application and appropriate scopes.
blockers: requires vetting process
LinkedIn Ads.notes: API access is gated by a vetting process; not fully self‑serve.

GoHighLevel.description: GoHighLevel offers a REST API v2.0 with OAuth 2.0 and Private Integration Token authentication. Developers can create private integrations and obtain tokens via the Developer's Marketplace. The API is well documented and self-serve.
GoHighLevel.mcp_notes: HighLevel MCP Server for Claude Desktop (https://github.com/HighLevelScaling/ghl-mcp-server) and HighLevel MCP Server guide (https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000005741-how-to-use-the-highlevel-mcp-server)
blockers: requires support ticket to create developer account
GoHighLevel.notes: Access model inferred as free_signup; may require a support ticket to obtain developer credentials.

Mailchimp.description: Mailchimp Marketing API provides REST endpoints for managing audiences, campaigns, and more. Authentication can be done via an API key (obtained by any Mailchimp account, including free tier) or OAuth 2 for user‑on‑behalf access.
Mailchimp.notes: OAuth 2 is required for integration partner program; API key works for self‑serve.

Klaviyo.description: Klaviyo offers private API key authentication for server-side APIs, OAuth for server-side APIs, and public key authentication for client-side APIs. API credentials can be obtained via self‑service signup. Comprehensive OpenAPI spec and Postman collection are provided.
Klaviyo.mcp_notes: Official remote‑hosted MCP server at https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp
Klaviyo.notes: Public key authentication is mentioned but not mapped to a standard auth method in schema.

systeme.io.description: Systeme.io provides a public REST API accessed via an X-API-Key header generated in user dashboard. API covers contacts, tags, funnels, courses, etc.
systeme.io.notes: Access model not specified; unclear if API key available on free tier.

Pinterest.description: Pinterest API v5 is a REST API covering pins, boards, catalogs, ads, audiences, and analytics. Access is tiered (Trial and Standard). Developers must create a business account, accept Developer Terms of Service, and submit an app request form for trial access; requests are reviewed each business day and apps can be approved or denied. Approved apps receive an app ID and app secret, and use OAuth with configured redirect URIs.
Pinterest.mcp_notes: Pinterest Engineering blog (Mar 2026) describes an internal MCP ecosystem with a central registry and production integrations. A third-party open-source MCP server exists: clugtu/pinterest-mcp (GitHub, MIT, Python) for API v5 (create pins, manage boards, analytics).
blockers: app request must be submitted and reviewed/approved (not instant)
requires business account + Developer ToS acceptance
Standard access requires upgrade beyond Trial
Pinterest.notes: Access is self-initiated (you submit the form yourself) but gated behind a manual review/approval process, so it is not fully self-serve. Auth uses OAuth (redirect URIs) plus app ID/secret. The MCP blog post is dated Mar 2026 and describes an internal ecosystem; the GitHub MCP is a small third-party project (0 stars). Worth double-checking whether the internal MCP registry is publicly accessible.

Threads (Meta).description: Threads (Meta) API lets developers create and publish posts, retrieve media and profiles, moderate replies, and access insights. Access requires creating a Meta app with the Threads use case, using the Threads app ID/secret, and users granting OAuth permissions (threads_basic, threads_content_publish, threads_manage_replies, threads_read_replies, threads_manage_insights). Free with no paid tier or per-call fee, but production access requires Meta App Review and calls are metered by a 4,800×impressions rate-limit formula with 24-hour caps (250 posts, 1000 replies, 100 deletions per profile).
Threads (Meta).mcp_notes: Multiple third-party MCP servers exist: sergekostenchuk/threads-mcp (OAuth, media, analytics) and poisonstefani-dev/threads-mcp (stdio MCP for official Threads API). Blotato also exposes Threads via its own MCP server.
blockers: Production access requires Meta App Review
Rate-limited (4,800×impressions formula, 24h caps: 250 posts/1000 replies/100 deletions)
Media must be hosted on a publicly accessible server
Threads (Meta).notes: Auth is OAuth2 (user grants permissions via Authorization Window) plus app ID/app secret (api_key). Testers can grant permissions at any time, but non-tester users require App Review for production. Free with no published fee. Rate limits are the main practical constraint rather than cost.

SendGrid.description: SendGrid provides a REST API that is authenticated using API keys. API keys can be created via the UI or via the /v3/api_keys endpoint. Basic authentication is deprecated and rejected. The API supports full, custom, and billing access scopes.
SendGrid.notes: API keys are the preferred authentication method; 2FA is required for account access. API keys can be scoped and revoked. No mention of free signup or paid tiers in the docs provided.

Shopify.description: Shopify provides OAuth 2.0 based access tokens (client ID/secret) for its REST and GraphQL APIs. Developers can create apps in the Dev Dashboard and obtain credentials without sales contact. Official MCP servers are documented for Storefront integration.
Shopify.notes: API key/secret are used for OAuth, not as direct API key authentication. Access model assumes developers can sign up as partners for free.

WooCommerce.description: WooCommerce REST API (WP REST API v3) connects a WooCommerce store to external systems. It exposes broad resources (products, variations, orders, order notes/refunds, customers, coupons, etc.) with create/retrieve/list/update/delete and batch operations. Access is controlled via per-user REST API keys (Consumer Key + Consumer Secret) generated in the WordPress admin (WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API) or auto-generated via an endpoint, with Read/Write/Read-Write permission levels.
WooCommerce.mcp_notes: Native MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration exists in WooCommerce, currently in developer preview. Documented at https://developer.woocommerce.com/docs/features/mcp/ and added via merged PR #60901 (woocommerce/woocommerce).
blockers: Requires an existing WooCommerce/WordPress store to generate keys
MCP integration is in developer preview (may change)
WooCommerce.notes: API keys are generated per WordPress user within a store, so a developer needs a WooCommerce site (self-hosted or hosted) to obtain credentials — not a central developer portal. Auth is via Consumer Key/Secret (API key style), not OAuth2. MCP is native but explicitly in developer preview, so integration details may change.

BigCommerce.description: BigCommerce provides OAuth2-based REST APIs with store-level, app-level, and account-level API accounts. Developers can create API credentials via the control panel or developer portal after signing up for a free sandbox store.
BigCommerce.notes: API access requires creating API accounts in the store UI; store owner permissions needed. Free sandbox store available for development.

Salesforce Commerce Cloud.description: Salesforce Commerce Cloud (B2C Commerce) provides a comprehensive RESTful SCAPI for storefront and admin functions, secured via OAuth2 client credentials through SLAS or Account Manager.
Salesforce Commerce Cloud.mcp_notes: B2C Commerce Model Context Protocol (MCP) Service – https://developer.sf.tumee.com/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/agentic-mcp-shopper-tools-quick-start.html
blockers: requires paid Commerce Cloud account
requires admin role to create API client
Salesforce Commerce Cloud.notes: API access is at no extra cost for existing Commerce Cloud customers, but requires a paid Commerce Cloud subscription and admin privileges to create API clients.

Magento (Adobe Commerce).description: Adobe Commerce (Magento) provides REST, GraphQL, and SOAP APIs. Authentication uses OAuth 1.0a for third‑party apps, token‑based for mobile apps, and login credentials for admins/customers. Access requires a Commerce Cloud (PaaS) subscription, typically via sales contact.
blockers: requires sales contact
requires Adobe Commerce Cloud subscription
Magento (Adobe Commerce).notes: OAuth 1.0a is not OAuth2; token auth maps to custom_token. No explicit self‑serve signup for API keys.

Squarespace.description: Squarespace Commerce APIs provide REST endpoints for managing commerce data. Authentication via API key or OAuth access token. Public documentation available.
Squarespace.notes: API appears self-serve for developers with a Squarespace site; no sales contact required.

Ecwid.description: Ecwid (by Lightspeed) provides a REST API for accessing and managing store data, products, orders, customers, payment/shipping methods, and storefront settings. It uses OAuth 2.0 for public apps and simplified non-expiring access tokens (public/secret) for custom single-store apps. Rate limit is 600 requests/minute per token.
Ecwid.mcp_notes: Multiple MCP servers found: viaSocket MCP Server for Ecwid (https://viasocket.com/mcp/ecwid-by-lightspeed) and a community-built 'Ecwid MCP' by ecwid-dev (https://mymcptools.com/servers/ecwid-mcp, though its GitHub repo could not be verified).
Ecwid.notes: No test mode exists; docs recommend a separate test store. Access tokens for custom apps do not expire. The ecwid-dev MCP entry is flagged as unverifiable (no resolvable GitHub repo).

Gumroad.description: Gumroad is a digital commerce platform for creators to sell e-books, courses, software, memberships, music, and physical goods. It offers a v2 REST API (OAuth-based) providing programmatic access to products, sales, subscribers, offer codes, license keys, customers, and the authenticated user account. The API is RESTful, returns JSON for all requests including errors, and uses OAuth 2.0 access tokens in the Authorization header. A Gumroad CLI is also available that wraps every endpoint.
Gumroad.mcp_notes: Two third-party MCP servers found: rmarescu/gumroad-mcp (10 stars, MIT, Go) and keithah/gumroad-mcp (JavaScript, for subscriptions/sales/products). No official MCP mentioned.
Gumroad.notes: The Verify License API endpoint does not require an OAuth application. APIs.io scores the API as 'thin' (28.4/100) with low developer ergonomics, but the official docs describe a broad set of endpoints (products, sales, subscribers, offer codes, license keys, customers) and a CLI, supporting a rich_rest rating. Access model inferred as free_signup since Gumroad is a free-to-start creator platform and the docs describe self-serve OAuth app registration with no mention of sales/approval gates.

Amazon Selling Partner.description: Amazon Selling Partner API (SP‑API) is a RESTful interface for Amazon sellers. It requires application registration and authorization via Login with Amazon (OAuth2). Public developers must list their app in the Amazon Selling Partner Appstore and undergo an architecture review with the SP‑API Solutions Architecture team before gaining access.
blockers: requires architecture review
no public API access without approval
Amazon Selling Partner.notes: Restricted operations use a Restricted Data Token (RDT) instead of the standard LWA token.

fanbasis.description: FanBasis (also branded "Commas") is a digital products & services marketplace for creators. Its public REST API (base https://www.fanbasis.com, sandbox https://qa.dev-fan-basis.com) covers checkout sessions, one-time payments, subscriptions, customers, products, discount codes, transactions, refunds, and webhook subscriptions. Auth is a single API key sent via the x-api-key header, with per-key scopes (e.g. checkout-sessions, refunds, payments, webhooks, customers). Webhooks use HMAC-SHA256 signature verification with a webhook secret. Separate test/live environments exist.
fanbasis.mcp_notes: Zapier MCP for FanBasis exists at https://zapier.com/mcp/fanbasis (triggers for disputes, failed payments, leads, Discord joins, manual transactions).
fanbasis.notes: Product is branded both "FanBasis" and "Commas" (Commas API Reference, base URL fanbasis.com). Access model inferred as freemium: docs say to log into the dashboard and copy an API key (self-serve, no sales/approval mentioned), but no explicit free-tier/pricing details are given, so freemium vs free_signup is uncertain. Auth is explicitly a single API key (no OAuth). API key scopes mean a key lacking a scope gets 403.

DataForSEO.description: DataForSEO offers a broad REST API (v3) for SEO and marketing data (SERP, keywords, backlinks, on-page, domain analytics, business data, etc.). The REST API uses HTTP Basic authentication (login:password) with credentials generated separately from the account password. A hosted MCP server is also available for AI agents.
DataForSEO.mcp_notes: Official DataForSEO MCP server exists: https://dataforseo.com/seo-mcp-server and GitHub repo dataforseo/mcp-server-typescript. Run via `npx dataforseo-mcp-server`. Hosted MCP server at mcp.dataforseo.com uses OAuth2 (authorizationCode flow).
DataForSEO.notes: Two distinct auth surfaces: the v3 REST API (api.dataforseo.com) uses HTTP Basic auth only (554 operations across 12 OpenAPI specs all declare basicAuth). OAuth2 (authorizationCode) exists only on the hosted MCP server (mcp.dataforseo.com), which is a separate host with its own authorization server. The API password is generated by DataForSEO and differs from the account password. Credentials are obtained at app.dataforseo.com/api-access after registering at app.dataforseo.com/register. The MCP server offers $1 free credit to start. The blog article mentions 'API key' in its table of contents but the actual auth mechanism is Basic auth (login:password), not a traditional API key.

SE Ranking.description: SE Ranking offers two REST APIs – Data API for raw SEO data and Project API for project management. Both are authenticated with a single UUID‑formatted API key. Data API usage is billed via a pay‑as‑you‑go credit system; Project API consumes subscription limits. API access is available to any plan that includes credits (Business/Enterprise or API add‑on) and a 14‑day free trial is offered for the API package. An MCP server is also available for AI agents.
SE Ranking.notes: Free 14‑day trial provides 100,000 credits; after trial, a paid plan is required for continued access.

Ahrefs.description: Ahrefs API v3 is a REST API at https://api.ahrefs.com/v3 exposing SEO/marketing data (Site Explorer, Keywords Explorer, Site Audit, Rank Tracker, SERP, Brand Radar, Web/Social analytics) across 148 operations in 13 tools, documented via a single OpenAPI 3.2.0 spec plus per-tool specs. Auth is a bearer API key (Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>); some public endpoints need no key. Access requires a paid Lite or higher subscription plan (Lite/Standard/Advanced/Enterprise), metered in API units. Also reachable via an official hosted MCP server and the OAuth-based Ahrefs Connect partner program.
Ahrefs.mcp_notes: Official hosted remote MCP server at https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/mcp (Streamable HTTP transport); requires Lite plan or higher.
blockers: requires paid Lite or higher subscription
no free API tier (only some public endpoints keyless)
Ahrefs.notes: OAuth2 is mentioned only for the Ahrefs Connect partner program, not the core API (which uses a bearer API key). self_serve set false because API access is gated behind a paid plan (Lite+), though a developer can self-serve a paid subscription without sales contact.

MrScraper.description: MrScraper is a web scraping platform offering a REST API for programmatically scraping web pages and retrieving structured data. The API uses predictable resource-oriented URLs, JSON request/response bodies, and standard HTTP response codes. It includes Platform, Marketplace, Travel, and Analytics endpoints.
MrScraper.mcp_notes: Official cloud-hosted MCP server documented at https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server. Also listed on Composio (https://composio.dev/toolkits/mrscraper).
blockers: Some endpoints on other hosts require contacting support for a separate API token
MrScraper.notes: Analytics endpoints use a different auth method (query parameters) than the standard x-api-token header. Access to endpoints on hosts other than the V3 Platform, Sync, and Analytics hosts requires contacting support. Token-based billing system where each plan includes a set number of tokens.

Apify.description: Apify is a platform for web scraping, AI agents, and automation. Its public API (v2) is a RESTful HTTP API with JSON responses, organized around resource-oriented URLs, with a downloadable OpenAPI schema (YAML/JSON) and official client libraries for Node.js, Python, Java, Rust, .NET, PHP, and Go. Authentication uses a Bearer API token.
Apify.mcp_notes: Official Apify MCP server exists at mcp.apify.com (GitHub: apify/apify-mcp-server, ~4892 stars, MIT). Enables AI agents to discover/run Actors, access storages/results, and access Apify docs.
Apify.notes: Auth is a Bearer API token (custom token / API key). The text does not explicitly state a free tier or pricing, so 'freemium' is inferred from Apify's known free plan; self_serve is true since a developer can create an account and obtain an API token without sales approval. The integrations page mentions contacting integrations@apify.com for platform-level collaboration, but that is for building integrations, not for getting API access.

Firecrawl.description: Firecrawl is a web scraping/crawling API that converts web pages into clean markdown/structured data for LLM applications. It offers endpoints for scrape, crawl, map, search, and extract (structured data via natural language). It handles proxies, caching, rate limits, JS-rendered content, PDFs, and images.
Firecrawl.mcp_notes: Official Firecrawl MCP Server exists: https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server/ (MIT, ~7.3k stars). Adds web scraping and search to Cursor, Claude, and other LLM clients.
Firecrawl.notes: A keyless free tier exists (rate-limited per IP) for scrape, search, and interact; all other methods require an API key. API key is obtained from firecrawl.dev. Auth is via Authorization: Bearer header with an fc- prefixed key.

Bright Data.description: Bright Data provides a RESTful API accessed via API key (Bearer token). API keys are auto-generated on account creation and can be managed by users. Documentation includes Dataset API and SERP API with clear examples.
Bright Data.notes: Native proxy authentication uses username/password but is not a standard HTTP auth method; primary public API uses API key.

Sherlock.description: Sherlock AI offers a RESTful API compatible with the OpenAI API format, authenticated via API keys that can be created directly in the control panel.
Sherlock.mcp_notes: Sherlock MCP for .NET (GitHub: jcucci/dotnet-sherlock-mcp) and NuGet package Sherlock.MCP.Server
Sherlock.notes: The product also has an EmailSherlock API for email verification, but the primary Sherlock AI API is the focus here.

Waterfall.io.description: Waterfall.io is a B2B data aggregation API that unifies 30+ data vendors to find/enrich contacts, verify emails, find mobile numbers, and track job changes. The REST API (base https://api.waterfall.io/v1/) offers endpoints for Prospector (async), Search Contact, Search Company, Contact Enrichment (async), Phone Enrichment (async), Company Enrichment (async), Company Reveal (beta), and Company Titles.
Waterfall.io.mcp_notes: No Waterfall-specific MCP server found; MCP search results were only generic OpenAI/Python SDK MCP docs.
blockers: no documented free self-serve signup/pricing for API key
access model/pricing not stated in provided docs
Waterfall.io.notes: Auth is clearly a single x-api-key header (API key). API is well-documented REST with both sync and async endpoints. However, the provided text does not state how to obtain an API key, whether there is a free tier/trial, or pricing, so self_serve and access_model are uncertain. Recommend verifying signup/pricing on waterfall.io.

Clay.description: Clay is a data enrichment and scraping platform. It offers a Public API for calling Clay from your own applications, plus an Agent Plugin (CLI + MCP server) for coding agents. The API key enables Clay-native integrations such as looking up single/multiple rows in tables. The MCP server exposes 150+ data providers, AI research agents, and prebuilt workflows to AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Codex).
Clay.mcp_notes: Official Clay MCP server exists. Docs: https://university.clay.com/docs/connect-to-clay-mcp and https://www.clay.com/guides/clay-mcp. Uses OAuth with Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) as the self-service path; also bundled in the Agent Plugin (CLI) for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor.
blockers: Agent Plugin/CLI is open beta (Mac/Linux only, no Windows)
Clay.notes: Access model inferred as freemium: a Clay account is required to obtain an API key (self-serve via Settings > Account > API key), and Clay is a commercial product with paid tiers; the text does not explicitly state a free tier, so this is a mild inference. The Agent Plugin/CLI is in open beta (Mac and Linux only, Windows unsupported). The Public API section in the quickstart was truncated, so full endpoint breadth is not fully confirmed, but the presence of a dedicated developers.clay.com site, llms.txt index, and MCP with 150+ providers supports a rich API.

GitHub.description: GitHub's REST API is a broad, well-documented API for creating integrations, retrieving data, and automating workflows. It supports standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE) and is accessible via CLI, curl, or JavaScript (Octokit.js SDK).
GitHub.mcp_notes: Official GitHub MCP Server exists at https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server (MIT licensed, ~32.7k stars).
GitHub.notes: Auth is via tokens (personal access tokens, GitHub App tokens, or GITHUB_TOKEN in Actions) passed in the Authorization header. JWTs must use 'Authorization: Bearer'.

Vercel.description: Vercel offers a broad, well-documented REST API (v1/v9/v10 endpoints) covering projects, domains, access groups, AI gateway, and more, plus a type-safe TypeScript SDK (@vercel/sdk). Authentication is via a Vercel access token. Vercel also provides Vercel Connect for third-party API access and an official Vercel MCP server for AI tool integration.
Vercel.mcp_notes: Official "Vercel MCP" server exists (vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp.md) — connects Vercel to AI tools, supports deploy, purchases, and the 2026-07-28 MCP spec. Vercel also supports deploying third-party MCP servers.
Vercel.notes: Auth is described as a "Vercel access token" (custom_token); no explicit OAuth2/API-key label given in the text. Access model inferred as free_signup since prerequisites only require a Vercel account and a token — no sales/partner gate mentioned. Vercel Connect (vercel.com/docs/connect) is a separate feature for connecting agents to third-party APIs (Slack, GitHub, Notion, etc.) and is not the Vercel API itself.

Netlify.description: Netlify is a hosting service for the programmable web. It provides a REST-style API (JSON serialization) to manage atomic deploys of websites/apps, manage form submissions, inject JavaScript snippets, manage DNS, and more. The API is documented via an OpenAPI/Swagger spec (v2.55.0/2.57.0) and uses OAuth 2 for authentication. Official Go and JS API clients are provided.
Netlify.mcp_notes: Official Netlify MCP server exists: https://github.com/netlify/netlify-mcp (netlify/netlify-mcp), announced in Netlify blog "Netlify MCP Server" (Agent Week). Enables code agents to use the Netlify API and CLI to create projects, build, deploy, and manage resources.
Netlify.notes: Auth is OAuth 2 (implicit flow per swagger securityDefinitions, authorizationUrl https://app.netlify.com/authorize). No API key method is explicitly mentioned in the provided text, so only oauth2 is listed. Access model inferred as free_signup since Netlify offers a free tier and self-serve OAuth app creation; not explicitly stated in the scraped text, so a human may want to confirm the free-tier API access details.

Cloudflare.description: Cloudflare offers a broad, versioned REST API (v4) for managing its infrastructure and data products (DNS, zones, accounts, etc.). Authentication is via API tokens (Bearer) or legacy API keys.
Cloudflare.mcp_notes: Cloudflare provides official documentation and SDKs to build and deploy MCP servers on its platform (https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/model-context-protocol/).
Cloudflare.notes: The text mentions 'API keys' as a legacy/less secure method and 'API tokens' as the preferred method. Both are mapped to api_key and custom_token respectively. The MCP search results indicate Cloudflare supports building MCP servers, but does not explicitly name a pre-built 'Cloudflare API MCP server' for third-party use, though the platform supports it.

Supabase.description: Supabase is an open-source Postgres platform that auto-generates REST API routes (GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE) from Postgres tables, views, and functions. Access is controlled via API keys (publishable/secret, with legacy anon/service_role JWT keys being deprecated by end of 2026) and Row Level Security. A Management API and CLI are also available.
Supabase.mcp_notes: Official Supabase MCP server exists: hosted at https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp and open-source repo github.com/supabase/mcp (Apache 2.0, ~2872 stars).
Supabase.notes: Legacy anon/service_role keys are JWT-based and being deprecated by end of 2026 in favor of publishable (sb_publishable_xxx) and secret (sb_secret_xxx) API keys. Both key types work simultaneously during migration.

Neo4j.description: Neo4j Aura provides a RESTful API (v1) accessible at https://api.neo4j.io. Authentication is via OAuth 2.0 Bearer tokens obtained through client credentials created in the Aura console. All tiers can create credentials, and the API is fully self‑serve with comprehensive documentation and an API specification. The API is rich, offering many endpoints for managing Aura instances.
Neo4j.notes: No free tier is explicitly documented; API access requires a paid Aura plan. The API is versioned and supports retries on 5xx responses.

Snowflake.description: Snowflake offers REST and SQL APIs that can be authenticated using key pair (JWT), OAuth, programmatic access tokens (PAT), and workload identity federation. The REST API includes endpoints for creating, fetching, and managing API integrations. Snowflake also provides a managed Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for AI agents.
Snowflake.notes: Workload identity federation authentication details are not fully described in the provided excerpts.

MongoDB Atlas.description: MongoDB Atlas Administration API is a versioned REST API for managing Atlas clusters, organizations, projects, and database users. It does not provide access to data stored in clusters (data access requires separate database user credentials). Authentication is via OAuth 2.0 Service Accounts (recommended) or legacy HTTP Digest API keys.
MongoDB Atlas.mcp_notes: Official MongoDB Atlas Managed MCP Server (GA, MongoDB-hosted, available as native plugin in Claude/ChatGPT/Cursor/Devin/Grok Build) plus community mongodb-js/mongodb-mcp-server (Apache 2.0, ~1121 stars).
blockers: API does not access cluster data (requires separate DB user credentials)
billing requires valid credit card on file
MongoDB Atlas.notes: API keys (HTTP Digest) are explicitly marked legacy; OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow is recommended. Service account client ID/secret can be created self-serve in the Atlas UI. Access model set to freemium since Atlas has a free tier but API-driven changes are subject to billing and require a credit card on file.

Datadog.description: Datadog provides a comprehensive REST API requiring API keys (and application keys) for authentication, with newer support for OAuth2, personal and service access tokens. API keys can be generated by users themselves. The API is well-documented and accessible to free-tier accounts.
Datadog.mcp_notes: Datadog MCP Server documented at https://docs.datadoghq.com/mcp_server.md
Datadog.notes: New authentication models (PATs, SATs, workload identity federation) are mentioned but not detailed; they likely map to token-based auth beyond API keys.

Sentry.description: Sentry provides a REST API authenticated via bearer tokens (user or organization auth tokens). Tokens can be created via the UI after signing up, with no sales or partnership required.
Sentry.notes: API tokens are static bearer tokens, not OAuth2. Free tier includes API access.

Notion.description: Notion provides a RESTful API authenticated via bearer tokens: OAuth 2.0 for public connections, static API tokens for internal connections and personal access tokens. Developers can create integrations in the Notion developer portal and obtain tokens themselves.
Notion.mcp_notes: Official MCP guide: https://developers.notion.com/guides/mcp/get-started-with-mcp (endpoint https://mcp.notion.com/mcp). Also third‑party npm package notion-mcp-server.
Notion.notes: Internal connections require workspace owner rights, but a personal workspace can be created for free to obtain a PAT.

Airtable.description: Airtable's public REST API (api.airtable.com/v0) uses token-based authentication via the HTTP Authorization Bearer header. It supports Personal Access Tokens (PATs) for personal/company development and OAuth access tokens for third-party integrations. Legacy API keys were deprecated as of Feb 1, 2024. PATs can be created self-serve at /create/tokens with granular scopes and base/workspace access.
Airtable.mcp_notes: Multiple third-party MCP servers exist, e.g. domdomegg/airtable-mcp-server (455 stars, npm: airtable-mcp-server) and rashidazarang/airtable-mcp (87 stars, airtablemcp.com).
Airtable.notes: Auth is token-based (PATs and OAuth access tokens) passed as Bearer tokens; the legacy api_key URL parameter is no longer supported. PATs are self-serve and free across all plan types, so a developer can get credentials today without sales approval. OAuth integration registration is also self-serve at /create/oauth.

Linear.description: Linear's public API is built using GraphQL (the same API used internally). It supports querying and mutating all entities (issues, projects, comments, etc.), with webhooks for push notifications. Authentication is via OAuth2 or personal API keys. A TypeScript SDK is available.
Linear.mcp_notes: Official Linear MCP server (centrally hosted, follows authenticated remote MCP spec) at https://linear.app/docs/mcp; also a third-party Efabien/linear-mcp-server on GitHub.
Linear.notes: Personal API keys can be created by Admins and permitted Members from Settings > Account > Security & Access; admins can always create keys. No mention of paid plan requirement for API access.

Jira.description: Jira Cloud offers a REST API (v2/v3) with comprehensive documentation. Authentication is supported via OAuth 2.0 (3LO) for apps, JWT for Connect apps, and basic authentication using an Atlassian account email and API token. Forge apps use OAuth 2.0 scopes. The API is well-documented and widely used for integration and automation.
Jira.notes: API token is used for basic auth; OAuth 2.0 3LO is recommended for security. MCP servers are third‑party implementations.

Asana.description: Asana provides a RESTful API with comprehensive documentation. Authentication is via personal access tokens (PAT) which act as API keys. Developers can obtain tokens through the developer console without sales interaction. An official MCP server is available for AI integrations.
Asana.mcp_notes: Asana MCP server documented at https://developers.asana.com/docs/using-asanas-mcp-server (also listed at https://onei.ai/mcps/asana)
Asana.notes: OAuth2 not mentioned in the provided excerpts, so only api_key is recorded. API access is free for any Asana user.

Monday.com.description: Monday.com provides a GraphQL API authenticated via personal API tokens (api_key style) and OAuth2. Tokens can be obtained by any user via the Developer Center, enabling self‑serve access. A hosted Platform MCP server is available at https://mcp.monday.com/mcp.
Monday.com.notes: API is GraphQL‑only; no REST endpoints mentioned.

ClickUp.description: ClickUp provides a public REST API (v2/v3) with personal API tokens and OAuth2 for apps. API is available on all plans, including free tier. Documentation is extensive and includes sample apps.
ClickUp.notes: Personal API token acts like an API key; OAuth2 required for multi-user apps. API endpoints may be limited by plan for some features.

Coda.description: Coda provides a public RESTful API for interacting with docs, tables, rows, etc. The API is available to all users without payment. An official MCP server exists at https://coda.io/apis/mcp using OAuth2.
Coda.mcp_notes: Official MCP server at https://coda.io/apis/mcp (public beta as of April 2026).
Coda.notes: Authentication method for the REST API not specified in provided docs; MCP uses OAuth2.

Smartsheet.description: Smartsheet provides a comprehensive REST API documented via OpenAPI. Authentication via OAuth2 or API token (bearer). API access limited to Business and Enterprise plans. MCP server exists for AI integration.
blockers: requires Business or Enterprise paid plan
Smartsheet.notes: API token generation is done in the Smartsheet UI; requires appropriate paid plan.

Harvest.description: Harvest V2 is a REST API for interacting with a Harvest account programmatically: track time, log expenses, create projects, manage clients, tasks, time entries, expenses, invoices, estimates, and users. Supports GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE, JSON or form-data bodies, and requires a Harvest-Account-Id header plus a User-Agent header.
Harvest.mcp_notes: Official Harvest MCP connection documented at https://support.getharvest.com/hc/en-us/articles/46293697226381-Harvest-MCP (start/stop timers, log hours, review time, check project budgets). Also a third-party MCP server: ianaleck/harvest-mcp-server (https://github.com/ianaleck/harvest-mcp-server), 60+ tools for clients, projects, time entries, invoices, reports.
Harvest.notes: Auth is OAuth2 or Personal Access Token (PAT); PAT is a custom token created from the Developers section of Harvest ID, replacing v1 Basic Auth. Access model set to freemium as a reasonable inference (Harvest has a free tier) but the scraped text does not explicitly state API access is free — worth double-checking whether API access requires a paid Harvest plan. The apis.io page also advertises a generic MCP endpoint (https://apis.io/mcp) that exposes the API to AI agents.

Stripe.description: Stripe's public REST API for payments, billing, customers, and financial operations. Uses API keys (secret, restricted, publishable) for authentication via HTTP Basic Auth or Bearer token.
Stripe.mcp_notes: Official Stripe MCP server exists (docs.stripe.com/mcp), installable via `stripe agent setup` CLI; also listed on mcp.directory as official.
Stripe.notes: Text explicitly mentions HTTP Basic Auth (API key as username) and Bearer auth. Test keys are freely available on signup; live keys require account verification but are still self-serve.

Plaid.description: Plaid is a financial data API that connects apps to bank accounts, providing access to transactions, balances, identity, assets, and more. The API is JSON over HTTPS (TLS 1.2), using POST requests. Authentication uses a client_id and secret (API key) sent in headers or body, plus OAuth 2.0 endpoints for token management.
Plaid.mcp_notes: Plaid offers two official MCP servers: a remote Dashboard MCP server (hosted by Plaid) for production diagnostics/analytics, and a local MCP server in the Plaid AI coding toolkit for development (mock data, doc search, sandbox tokens, webhook simulation). Also a third-party sandbox MCP: github.com/argotdev/plaid-mcp-python.
blockers: Production access requires an application/approval flow
Europe only offers Custom (sales) plans
Some products (Payment Initiation, Signal, Transfer) are Custom-plan only
Plaid.notes: Free Trial plan (10 Production Items) is available for new US/Canada teams on or after April 15, 2026; before that date or for other regions, Production access requires an application/approval flow. Europe only offers Custom (sales) plans. Some products (Payment Initiation, Signal Transaction Scores, Transfer) are Custom-plan only.

Binance.description: Binance offers a public REST and WebSocket API that can be accessed by creating an API key and secret after completing identity verification and enabling 2FA. The API supports trading, wallet, and market data operations.
Binance.notes: API key creation requires 2FA, a deposit to the Spot wallet, and identity verification.

Paygent Connect.description: Paygent (Paygentic) is a fintech platform for AI agents to earn, send, and manage money. It exposes a REST API (base https://api.paygent.to/api/v1 and api.paygentic.io) for managing products/tenants, users, subscriptions, and payments. API keys are environment-specific (sk_test_ sandbox / sk_live_ live) and used as Bearer tokens. A third-party SDK (paygentic-sdk) provides a typed REST client and an MCP server with 13 tools.
Paygent Connect.mcp_notes: Third-party MCP server exists: paygentic-sdk by FoxRick (https://github.com/FoxRick/paygentic-sdk, also listed on Glama at https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/FoxRick/paygentic-sdk). Run via `npx paygentic-sdk`, exposes 13 tools.
Paygent Connect.notes: Two distinct domains appear: docs.paygent.to (base https://api.paygent.to/api/v1, keys prefixed pg_live_) and docs.paygentic.io (api.paygentic.io, keys sk_test_/sk_live_). These may be the same product under different branding or two related services — worth verifying. The paygent.to docs describe a 'small REST API' (limited scope). The MCP server is third-party (0 stars, single contributor), not official.

iPayX.description: iPayX offers a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for forensic FX audit. The API is publicly accessible over HTTP with no authentication required and is free to use. It provides tools such as check_fx_rate, audit_transaction, and forensic report generation. Users can sign up for a free account or use the audit directly without signup. The MCP endpoint is hosted at https://mcp.ipayx.ai/mcp and also available via a Cloudflare Workers endpoint.
iPayX.mcp_notes: MCP server: https://mcp.ipayx.ai/mcp (official) – also hosted at https://wild-bird-a412.ybolduc.workers.dev/mcp
iPayX.notes: API is MCP, not a traditional REST or GraphQL API, so classification is marked as unknown.

QuickBooks.description: QuickBooks Online (QBO) public API. Authentication is via OAuth 2.0 (Intuit OAuth 2.0 server); developers create an app on the Intuit Developer Portal to obtain Client ID/Client secret, then use the authorization code flow to get access tokens tied to a user's QBO company (realmID). OpenID Connect is available for SSO. TLS 1.2+ required.
QuickBooks.mcp_notes: Official Intuit MCP server exists: intuit/quickbooks-online-mcp-server (GitHub, Apache 2.0, ~357 stars). A hosted MCP server (IntuitDeveloper/intuit-3p-ai-pilot) is in PILOT/Limited Availability for Intuit App Partner Program partners only.
QuickBooks.notes: Docs only cover auth (OAuth 2.0); the REST API breadth is inferred from the well-known QBO API but not detailed in the provided text, so api_quality=rich_rest is a reasonable but slightly extrapolated call. The hosted MCP server is gated to pilot partners, but the open-source MCP server is publicly available.

Xero.description: Xero provides a comprehensive REST API accessed via OAuth 2.0. Developers can sign up for a free Xero account, register an app to obtain client credentials, and start using the API immediately via the API Explorer. An official Xero MCP Server implementation exists.
Xero.notes: Custom Connections use client credentials grant, but standard OAuth2 flow is available for all developers.

Brex.description: Brex offers a RESTful API defined via OpenAPI with JSON over HTTPS. Authentication uses bearer tokens (user tokens) generated in the Brex dashboard and OAuth tokens for partner apps. Access requires a Brex account admin to accept the developer agreement and create a token, so not open self‑serve. An official MCP server exists (beta) at https://api.brex.com/mcp supporting OAuth with Dynamic Client Registration.
Brex.mcp_notes: Official MCP server endpoint: https://api.brex.com/mcp (OAuth with Dynamic Client Registration, beta).
blockers: requires Brex account admin to generate token
not publicly self‑serve
Brex.notes: API is rich but gated behind account admin; no free public signup.

Ramp.description: Ramp's Developer API is a REST API for expense management, card transactions, reimbursements, and related finance workflows. It uses OAuth 2.0 with multiple grant types (Client Credentials for internal/server-to-server, Authorization Code for third-party apps, Refresh Token). Access tokens are obtained from /developer/v1/token using HTTP Basic Auth (base64 client_id:client_secret). Sandbox (demo-api.ramp.com) and production (api.ramp.com) environments are available.
Ramp.mcp_notes: Official Ramp MCP server exists: ramp-public/ramp_mcp on GitHub (MIT, Python, 34 stars). NOTE: repo status is ARCHIVED. Also referenced in Ramp's own docs as "Ramp's MCP server" for Claude/ChatGPT/Cursor.
blockers: Requires existing Ramp customer account with admin access to create developer app
Sandbox access must be requested (not self-serve)
Ramp.notes: The getting-started guide explicitly states "This guide assumes you are a Ramp customer with admin access to your dashboard" and sandbox access must be requested. This means you cannot self-serve API credentials without first becoming a Ramp customer (which requires sales/onboarding). The API itself is well-documented and rich (OAuth 2.0, scopes, multiple grant types, sandbox+prod). The official MCP server repo is archived, which may indicate it's been superseded or is no longer maintained — worth verifying current status.

PitchBook.description: PitchBook (a Morningstar company) offers a RESTful API for direct, real-time access to its database of Companies, Deals, People, Investors, Funds, Service Providers, and Limited Partners. The API is a separate, paid, contract-gated offering from the PitchBook platform. It uses a static API key (Authorization: PB-Token header) with per-request credit billing. A test sandbox environment exists but requires a key from an account manager.
PitchBook.mcp_notes: Official PitchBook Premium remote MCP server at https://premium.mcp.pitchbook.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth auth). Also listed on apigene.ai as an official PitchBook MCP server.
blockers: requires standalone paid contract agreement
API key provisioned only via account manager, not self-serve
no free tier; per-request credit billing
sandbox key also requires account manager request
PitchBook.notes: API is described as RESTful with a broad data scope (rich_rest), but access is fully gated behind a paid contract and account-manager-issued API key, so it is not buildable today without a sales/contract process. An official hosted MCP server exists (OAuth-based), which may offer a different access path than the raw REST API, but the MCP is also 'Premium' and likely tied to the same paid access.

NotebookLM.description: NotebookLM provides a Google Cloud‑based API accessed via gcloud CLI or OAuth2, with unofficial Node.js/TypeScript and Python REST wrappers available.
blockers: requires Google Cloud account
NotebookLM.notes: Access model unclear; may require a paid plan or free tier.

Otter AI.description: Otter.ai offers two official programmatic surfaces: a Public API (channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines, workspace details, webhooks, file ingestion) and a hosted MCP server (read-only: search meetings, fetch transcripts, get current user). The Public API is gated to Enterprise workspaces and uses Bearer API keys (max 2 per user, 10 req/s). The MCP server connects from a standard Otter account over OAuth.
Otter AI.mcp_notes: Official hosted MCP server at https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth). Also referenced in Otter blog "Otter for Enterprise: Connect AI-to-AI with Otter's MCP" and Scalekit's comparison article.
blockers: Public API requires Enterprise workspace
contact account manager if feature not visible
no free self-serve API key for Public API
Otter AI.notes: Access model is inverted vs. most tools: the MCP server is available on a standard Otter account (OAuth), while the Public API is gated to Enterprise workspaces (Bearer API keys only, no OAuth). The third source (help.otterly.ai) is about a different product (OtterlyAI, an AI search visibility tool) and is NOT about Otter.ai — ignore for this app.

Fathom.description: Fathom is an AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes, and summarizes meetings. It offers a public REST API for accessing meeting insights (summaries, transcripts, action items), with API-key auth at the user level and OAuth 2.0 for building multi-account integrations. Official TypeScript and Python SDKs are provided, and an official MCP server connects Fathom meeting data to AI assistants.
Fathom.mcp_notes: Official Fathom MCP server documented at https://developers.fathom.ai/mcp-docs (connects to ChatGPT, Claude, etc.). A third-party MCP also exists: github.com/Dot-Fun/fathom-mcp (MIT, Python/FastMCP).
blockers: OAuth app requires registration/approval before use
rate limit capped at 60 calls/min with no higher limits offered
Fathom.notes: API keys are created at the user level and only access meetings recorded by or shared to that user/team; admin keys do not grant access to other users' unshared meetings. OAuth is intended for partners building marketplace integrations and requires registering an app first. Fathom is free to sign up, so free_signup is assumed, though the text does not explicitly state pricing.

Consensus.description: Consensus offers a RESTful API for programmatic access to peer‑reviewed research citations. The v1 API is accessed via an API key passed in the XApiKeyHeader, while the newer v2 API uses OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE. The API is documented with an OpenAPI spec and includes a quick_search endpoint. An MCP server is also available for Model Context Protocol integration.
Consensus.notes: OAuth 2.0 is required for V2; API key is used for V1. The MCP server is a separate, secure bridge for LLMs.

Reducto.description: Reducto is an agentic document platform offering a single API to parse, extract, classify, split, and edit 30+ file types into structured JSON. It provides Python, Node.js, and Go SDKs plus a REST API (POST https://platform.reducto.ai/parse). Developers sign up at studio.reducto.ai to create API keys.
Reducto.mcp_notes: Official Reducto MCP server exists: docs at https://docs.reducto.ai/mcp-server and GitHub repo https://github.com/reductoai/mcp-server-reducto. Supports local and hosted MCP for clients like Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf.
Reducto.notes: Access model inferred as freemium: docs show self-serve sign-up and API key creation, but no explicit free-tier/pricing details in the provided text. Auth is API-key based (REDUCTO_API_KEY env var); no OAuth/JWT mentioned. An official MCP server is documented, so agent integration is straightforward.

Devin.description: Devin provides a REST API with organization and enterprise scopes, authenticated via service user API keys or personal access tokens.
Devin.notes: API uses role-based access control; enterprise API is for enterprise customers only.

higgsfield.description: Higgsfield offers a RESTful asynchronous generative media API with over 100 model endpoints. Authentication is via an API key and secret passed in the Authorization header. The API supports image, video, audio, and 3D content generation, with status polling and webhook notifications. A self‑serve API key can be created in Higgsfield Cloud, and the documentation provides clear examples and endpoint listings.
higgsfield.notes: Pricing details are not provided in the docs; the presence of invoice-based billing suggests a paid plan is required.

Mermaid CLI.description: Mermaid CLI (mermaid-js/mermaid-cli) is an open-source command-line tool that takes a Mermaid diagram definition file as input and generates SVG/PNG/PDF output, with basic support for converting Mermaid code blocks in Markdown. It is a local CLI (installed via npm or Docker), not a hosted service. Note: the docs.rs and noahsabaj sources describe a different, unrelated project also named "Mermaid" (an AI pair-programmer CLI); the canonical mermaid-cli is the diagram renderer.
Mermaid CLI.mcp_notes: Two third-party MCP servers found: andrewginns/mermaid-mcp-server (Python wrapper over mermaid-cli for validating diagrams) and rtuin/mcp-mermaid-validator (validates and renders Mermaid diagrams).
blockers: no hosted/public REST API — local CLI only
requires Node.js/Puppeteer or Docker to run
Mermaid CLI.notes: Name collision: the docs.rs (mermaid-cli 0.25.0) and noahsabaj/mermaid-cli sources describe an AI pair-programmer terminal tool, NOT the mermaid-js diagram CLI. The authoritative mermaid-cli is the mermaid-js diagram renderer. The product is a local CLI with no hosted/public API; programmatic use is via the mmdc command or the underlying Mermaid JS library. No auth is involved.

YouTube Transcript.description: YouTube Transcript API (youtubetranscript.dev) — a REST API to extract, transcribe (ASR), and translate YouTube video transcripts at scale. Supports captions, audio transcription, batch processing, channel resolution, and 100+ languages. Has an official Python SDK and an OpenAPI spec.
YouTube Transcript.mcp_notes: Third-party MCP servers exist for YouTube transcripts (not this specific API): kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript (575 stars) and toorop/youtube-transcript-mcp (uses yt-dlp). No official MCP for youtubetranscript.dev found in the given text.
YouTube Transcript.notes: Auth is via API key (Python SDK takes "your_api_key"; docs say "Get your free API key at youtubetranscript.dev/dashboard"). Access model inferred as freemium: free API key is offered, and a Pricing page is linked, but the text does not explicitly detail free-tier limits vs paid tiers. The MCP servers found are generic YouTube-transcript tools (yt-dlp based), not integrations with this specific API — verify if an official MCP exists.

Grain.description: Grain is an AI notetaker for sales/customer meetings. Its public API lets developers read meeting data (recordings, transcripts, AI notes, action items, participants, tags, teams), manage recordings (upload, metadata, tags, sharing), download recordings/transcripts in multiple formats, and receive real-time webhook events. Auth is via Personal Access Token (PAT), Workspace Access Token (WAT), or OAuth2 Authorization Code flow (with PKCE). A v1 API is being sunset in favor of v2.
Grain.mcp_notes: Official Grain MCP server exists (released June 18, 2025) at https://api.grain.com/_/mcp, OAuth-authenticated, ~22 tools; also available as a Claude Connector. See support.grain.com/en/articles/14811968-grain-mcp.
blockers: OAuth2 client registration requires a redirect URI prefix
v1 API being sunset; some v1 features not carried to v2
Grain.notes: The third source (docs.grainql.com) is a DIFFERENT product (GrainQL, a query/event API using X-API-Key) and should NOT be conflated with Grain (grain.com). Its API-key/JWT details were excluded from this extraction. Grain's PAT is available on Starter plan and above; WAT grants access to ALL workspace data. OAuth2 requires registering a client with a redirect URI prefix.
